note: How the sampler plays recorded instruments (doc 24, Sampler rules). defaults apply to every instrument; byInstrument overrides any field for one instrument id. layers: bounds are the velocities (1..127) where one recorded layer hands over to the next (empty means evenly split), fadeWidth the number of velocity steps over which two layers crossfade (doc 24: 12), so a slow crescendo has no steps, and law the blend curve: 0 a straight-line blend (right for recordings that are in phase), 1 equal power (right for unrelated ones); two recordings of one key sit between, so judge it by ear on the bench's close-up test. velocity: the attack loudness rebuilt from velocity because the library's files are normalized one by one: floorDb at velocity 1, topDb at 127, gamma the curve's shape (above 1 keeps soft playing soft longer). register: a gentle balance in dB (bassDb at the lowest A, trebleDb at the top C, 0 at pivotMidi). brightness: a lowpass that opens with velocity, lowHz at pp to highHz at f, never below minHarmonic times the note's fundamental. tuning: policy is recorded (as the piano was tuned, with its own stretch), equal (every zone pulled to equal temperament at A4 = 440 Hz, doc 24's rule) or stretch (pulled onto a gentle stretch curve, bassCents at the lowest A and trebleCents at the top C, 0 at pivotMidi); zones measured with less confidence than minConfidence stay as recorded. dampers: how fast a released key is stopped, a time constant from bassS to trebleS; keys at or above undampedFromMidi have no damper and ring on, as on a real grand. release: how loud the key-off sound plays relative to the note (dB) and how short notes make it louder. retrigger: a repeated key damps the old string over this many seconds (doc 24: 80 ms). stealing: the most voices at once per tier, and the fade when one is stolen (doc 24: 30 ms, never a click); decay rates guess each voice's current loudness. load: maxTailS trims long tails when files are decoded (0 keeps all), monoBelowMidi folds notes below that key to mono (0 for none), sets to load. pedalNoise: the recorded pedal mechanism (from the Knight upright) under any piano, its level in dB, or off.
